title: Blocking Abundant RNA Transcripts by High-Affinity Oligonucleotides during Transcriptome Library Preparation
author: Everaert, Verwilt, et al.
materials: RPMI 1640 medium with GlutaMAX supplement (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA, 61870010)
Chromium GemCode Single Cell Instrument (10x Genomics, Pleasonton, CA, USA, 1000204)
Direct cDNA sequencing kit (Oxford Nanopore Technologies, UK, SQK-DCS109)
Eppendorf Protein LoBind microcentrifuge tubes (Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany, Z666548)
Ficoll Paque Plus (Cytiva, Washington, D.C., USA, 17144002)
Flongle Flow cell (Oxford Nanopore Technologies, UK, FLO-FLG001)
Fragment Analyzer RNA Kit (Agilent, USA, DNF-471-0500)
GemCode Chip G (10x Genomics, Pleasonton, CA, USA, 2000177)

Total RNA was isolated from platelet-free (PFP) and platelet-rich plasma (PRP) using the miRNeasy Serum/Plasma Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany, 217,184). We used 200 μl of plasma as input. For the cancer patient experiment, 2 μl of 1x RC PFP spikes were added to the plasma during isolation. The elution volume was 14 μl, and we added 2 μl of 1x LP PFP spikes (Thermo Fisher). Detailed descriptions of the spike-in controls can be found in the exRNAQC study [50]. From this total volume, we used 5 μl for the library preparation. For the healthy donor experiment, the eluate of multiple parallel extractions was pooled according to the original biofluid type (PRP or PFP) and split into six aliquots of 5 μl to minimize extraction bias. We did not include a gDNA removal step after RNA isolation. The input is volume-based since the RNA concentrations of PFP and PRP are below the limit of quantification.

We used HEK293T cells that were grown in RPMI 1640 medium with GlutaMAX supplement (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum (Merck, Germany) and were lysed with SingleShot lysis buffer (Bio-Rad, United States of America).
to investigate the quality of the reads.

We extracted RNA using the RNeasy Micro Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany, 217,184) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. We checked the quality of the RNA (RQN = 10) using a Fragment Analyzer (Agilent, United States of America).

We collected whole blood in EDTA tubes. The blood was transferred to Leucosep filtered tubes (Greiner Bio-One) containing 15 ml of Ficoll Paque Plus (Cytiva, Washington, D.C., USA, 17144002) and diluted (1:2) with the same volume of 1X DPBS (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA, 14190144). We centrifuged the samples at room temperature for 18 minutes at 800 rcf and extracted the PBMCs from the resulting buffy coat. The extracted PBMCs were centrifuged and washed twice with 1X DPBS (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA, 14190144). We took a sample for counting, and assessed the cell viability and concentration with a Neubauer chamber, counting at least two different squares. PBMCs were then resuspended in freezing mix (complete medium (RPMI + 1% pen/strep + 10% FCS) + 10% DMSO) in cryovials with no more than 10 million cells. The vials were stored first at − 80 °C inside a freezing container for 24 h and then at − 150 °C. We thawed the vials just before live-death sorting.

steps.title: Isolate plasma RNA with miRNeasy
steps.instruction: Use the miRNeasy Serum/Plasma Kit (Qiagen, cat. 217,184) on 200 µl of plasma; for cancer samples add 2 µl of 1× RC PFP spike‑in during isolation, elute RNA in 14 µl, then add 2 µl of 1× LP PFP spike‑in (Thermo Fisher); pool eluates for healthy donors as described and split into six 5 µl aliquots; do not perform a gDNA removal step; use 5 µl of each eluate for downstream library preparation.

steps.title: Culture HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Grow HEK293T cells in RPMI 1640 medium with GlutaMAX (Thermo Fisher) supplemented with 10 % fetal calf serum (Merck) until 80 % confluence in a T75 flask.

steps.title: Harvest and lyse HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Wash cells with 2 ml Versene, incubate with 2 ml trypsin for 3 min at 37 °C, neutralize with 8 ml fresh medium, centrifuge 5 min at 2000 rcf at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 ml QIAzol and flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Extract cellular RNA with RNeasy Micro
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from the frozen QIAzol lysate using the RNeasy Micro Kit (Qiagen, cat. 217,184) according to the manufacturer’s protocol; assess RNA quality (RQN = 10) on an Agilent Fragment Analyzer.

steps.title: Prepare direct‑cDNA Nanopore library
steps.instruction: Follow the SQK‑DCS109 Kit (Oxford Nanopore Technologies) protocol with the following modifications: bind RNA to beads for 5 min on a Hula Mixer then 5 min at room temperature; elute RNA from beads for 5 min at 37 °C then 5 min on a Hula Mixer at room temperature; wash beads with 300 µl 80 % ethanol.

steps.title: Basecall and process Nanopore reads
steps.instruction: Basecall raw fast5 files with Guppy v3.5.2 on a GPU; group reads per sample; run Pychopper v2.3.1 to select full‑length transcripts containing both primers; map reads with Minimap2 v2.11; extract reads mapping to the target fragment using SAMtools v1.11; evaluate read length and quality with NanoComp v1.12.0.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs from whole blood
steps.instruction: Collect whole blood in EDTA tubes, transfer to Leucosep tubes containing 15 ml Ficoll‑Paque Plus (Cytiva, cat. 17144002) and dilute 1:2 with 1× DPBS (Thermo Fisher, cat. 14190144); centrifuge at room temperature for 18 min at 800 rcf; collect PBMCs from the buffy coat, wash twice with 1× DPBS, count cells using a Neubauer chamber (count at least two squares) and assess viability.

steps.title: Freeze PBMCs for later use
steps.instruction: Resuspend PBMCs in freezing mix (RPMI + 1 % pen/strep + 10 % FCS + 10 % DMSO) at ≤10 million cells per cryovial; place vials at –80 °C in a controlled‑rate freezing container for 24 h, then transfer to –150 °C; thaw immediately before live‑death sorting.

steps.title: Prepare single‑cell 10x library
steps.instruction: Resuspend sorted single‑cell suspensions in PBS + 0.04 % BSA at ~1000 cells/µl; load onto a Chromium GemCode Single Cell Instrument (10x Genomics) using Chip G (cat. #2000177) to generate GEMs; construct scRNA‑seq libraries with the GemCode Single Cell 3′ Gel Bead and Library kit, version NextGEM 3.1 (PN‑1000121) following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Demultiplex and count 10x reads
steps.instruction: Run cellranger mkfastq v6.0.1 to demultiplex BCL files, then run cellranger count v6.0.1 to obtain gene‑count matrices per cell.

steps.title: Trim, map and count small‑RNA reads
steps.instruction: Trim adapters and poly(A) tails with Cutadapt v1.8.1 (discard reads <15 nt or without adapter), filter low‑quality reads using FASTX‑Toolkit v0.0.14 (minimum Q20 in ≥80 % bases), remove spike‑in reads, then map remaining reads with Bowtie v1.1.2 allowing one mismatch; annotate mapped reads against miRBase v20 and other small‑RNA annotations from UCSC GRCh37/hg19 and Ensembl v84.

steps.title: Downsample and submit sequencing data
steps.instruction: Downsample each sample to the read count of the lowest‑depth sample (or to 13 M reads for the concentration experiment, 6.5 M reads for the modification experiment, and 7 M reads for the cancer experiment); submit original FASTQ files and count tables to EGA (accession EGAS00001006023).

steps.title: Run differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: In R v3.6.0, load tidyverse v1.2.1, biomaRt v2.40.4, and broom v0.5.2; filter the count matrix to retain miRNAs with ≥10 RPM in all samples; perform limma‑voom v3.40.6 differential expression analysis.

steps.title: Process FASTQ files for QuantSeq libraries
steps.instruction: Trim poly(A) tails and adapters with BBMap v38.26, perform quality trimming, then subsample each FASTQ to 2,000,000 reads using Seqtk v1.3; map reads to hg38 with STAR v2.6.0, count reads mapping to LNA‑targeted regions with SAMtools v1.9, and generate overall counts with htseq‑count v0.11.0; assess read quality before and after trimming with FastQC v0.11.9.

steps.title: Analyze computational results
steps.instruction: Use R v4.1.0 with tidyverse v1.3.1 and biomaRt v2.48.3 for data analysis and visualization; for single‑cell data, load count matrices into Seurat v4.0.3 (no cell filtering) and visualize with tidyverse.
